question.problem: Find the equation for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence if the $6$th term is $-\frac{1}{5}$ and the common ratio is $-\frac{1}{5}.$
question.worked_solution:
The common ratio is $r=-\frac{1}{5},$ so we can start writing the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(-\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we still need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}.$ We know that the $6$th term is ${a}_{6}=-\frac{1}{5},$ so we can solve for the first term as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{6} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(-\frac{1}{5})}^{6-1} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(-\frac{1}{5})}^{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & =-{a}_{1}\cdot {(\frac{1}{5})}^{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & =-{a}_{1}\cdot (\frac{1}{{5}^{5}}) \\ {5}^{4} & ={a}_{1} \\ 625 & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know the first term is ${a}_{1}=625,$ we can complete the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {(-\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1} \\  & =625\cdot {(-\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$
